question:
A previously healthy 41-year-old woman comes to the physician for the evaluation of recurrent episodes of palpitations and sweating over the past month. Her symptoms typically start after swimming practice and improve after drinking ice tea and eating some candy. She has also had a 5-kg (11-lb) weight gain over the past 3 months. She works as a nurse. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Fasting serum studies show:
Glucose 38 mg/dL
Insulin 260 μU/mL (N=11–240)
Proinsulin 65 μU/mL (N <20% of total insulin)
C-peptide 5.0 ng/mL (N=0.8–3.1)
Insulin secretagogues absent
Which of the following is the most likely cause of her symptoms?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Peripheral resistance to insulin -> Increased insulin secretion -> Hypoglycemia symptoms -> 80% CHAIN: Exogenous administration of insulin -> High insulin levels -> Hypoglycemia symptoms -> 70% CHAIN: Factitious use of sulfonylureas -> Increased insulin secretion -> Hypoglycemia symptoms -> 75% CHAIN: Pancreatic β-cell tumor -> Increased insulin secretion -> Hypoglycemia symptoms -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most likely cause of the symptoms in the 41-year-old woman is a pancreatic β-cell tumor, leading to increased insulin secretion and subsequent hypoglycemia. This aligns with the evidence path showing that insulin can cause hypoglycemia. Exogenous administration of insulin, factitious use of sulfonylureas, and peripheral resistance to insulin are less likely causes in this context.
analysis: The core medical principle guiding this case is the evaluation of hypoglycemia in a patient with recurrent palpitations and sweating. Given the fasting serum studies showing low glucose levels, high insulin levels, and elevated proinsulin and C-peptide levels, along with the contextual information suggesting a pancreatic β-cell tumor, the most likely cause of her symptoms is a pancreatic β-cell tumor leading to hyperinsulinemia and subsequent hypoglycemia.
